headline: Microsoft surges 3.3% last night on AI earnings momentum, while CBA drops 2% at today's close in a rough session for the ASX.

portfolio.summary: A mixed day across the portfolio. CBA was the standout loser on the ASX today, dropping over 2% — likely dragged down by cooling rate-hike expectations after softer inflation data (less rate pain is usually good for borrowers but can compress bank profit margins). VGE also took a solid hit, down 1.6%. On the US side (last night's session), Microsoft was the star, jumping 3.3% on continued AI revenue enthusiasm. GOOGL edged up slightly, TTWO barely moved.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Big jump last night — AI revenue story is gaining momentum, with analysts suggesting Microsoft's AI income may actually be larger than what's being reported. The Build Conference is also in focus with a new AI coding model announcement.

movers.name: Commonwealth Bank
movers.note: Dropped $3.40 to close at $161.41 today. Softer-than-expected inflation data is making traders think the RBA won't raise rates as much — which can squeeze bank lending margins over time.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Down 1.6% at today's close to $91.50. Emerging markets remain sensitive to global risk sentiment and a slightly softer Aussie dollar.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy ETF
movers.note: Small dip to $8.60 today despite oil holding relatively steady. Middle East tensions (Strait of Hormuz risk) are in the background but haven't been enough to push energy stocks higher today.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: Edged down 0.5% to $75.40 today — nothing dramatic, just tracking the mild ASX softness.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Basically flat last night at $217.61. GTA 6 hype continues but the stock is treading water ahead of the release.

markets.summary: Last night on Wall Street, both major US indices pushed higher — the NASDAQ had a particularly good session, up 0.91%, driven largely by tech and AI names. Gold had a standout night, jumping over 2% to $4,537 USD/oz, suggesting investors are still a bit nervous and looking for safe havens. Oil was roughly flat. The AUD barely moved, sitting around 71.7 US cents. ASX 200 data wasn't available at time of writing — the index had a rough day based on how individual stocks performed.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's session — solid gains, broad-based rally.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Last night — tech led the charge, Microsoft a big contributor.

indicators.name: Gold (WTI)
indicators.note: Big move last night — gold surging as investors seek safety amid geopolitical uncertainty.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Essentially flat last night despite ongoing Middle East tensions.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Barely budged — Aussie dollar holding steady near 71.7 US cents.

politics.summary: Two big themes in Australian politics today: the Albanese government is pushing ahead with tax reform legislation, and softer inflation data is shifting expectations around interest rates — with bond markets now pricing in only one more RBA rate rise rather than several.

stories.title: Inflation surprise cools rate-hike bets
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's latest inflation print came in softer than expected, meaning prices aren't rising as fast as feared. Bond markets — which are basically the big money bets on where interest rates are going — have now dialled back their expectations, pricing in just one more RBA rate hike rather than multiple rises. For everyday Aussies with mortgages, this is welcome news: the end of the rate-rise cycle looks closer than it did a month ago. For CBA and other bank shareholders, it's a bit more nuanced — fewer rate hikes can eventually pressure bank profit margins.

stories.title: Government introduces first tranche of tax reform legislation
stories.why_it_matters: The Albanese government has introduced the first tranche (first instalment) of its tax reform legislation into parliament. The package is contentious — businesses say they're still negotiating but the government appears to be moving ahead regardless. The reforms are expected to include changes that affect how investments and properties are taxed, though the full details of this tranche are still emerging. Worth watching if you hold investment properties or assets with capital gains.

stories.title: Sky News host accuses government of 'ramming through' tax changes
stories.why_it_matters: Sky News host Sharri Markson is accusing the Albanese government of pushing through 'highly contentious' tax changes too quickly, despite the government's assurance that it's still in negotiation with the business community. The political fight over these reforms is heating up — the government is trying to sell them as fair while critics say businesses haven't had enough say. If the legislation changes how capital gains tax (CGT) — the tax you pay when you sell an asset for a profit — or negative gearing works, it could directly affect property investors and share traders.

ai.summary: A big day in AI news. Anthropic has launched a new flagship model that it claims beats both OpenAI and Google's latest offerings. Meanwhile, Microsoft is doubling down on AI coding tools at its Build conference — good news for MSFT holders. And a new study finds that basically every major AI model on the market is breaking EU rules.

stories.title: Anthropic launches Claude Opus 4.8, claims it beats GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro
stories.why_it_matters: Anthropic — the AI company backed partly by Google — has released Claude Opus 4.8, its most powerful model yet. The company claims it outperforms OpenAI's GPT-5.5 and Google's Gemini 3.1 Pro on benchmarks (standardised tests used to compare AI performance). This is relevant for GOOGL holders: Google's AI division is under increasing competitive pressure from both Anthropic (which Google itself funds) and OpenAI. The AI race is moving extremely fast, and being second-best even briefly can cost market share.

stories.title: Microsoft to launch new AI coding model at Build Conference
stories.why_it_matters: Microsoft is using its annual Build developer conference to unveil a new AI model specifically designed for writing and improving code. This is a direct push into one of the most commercially valuable AI use cases — software development. Analysts are already suggesting Microsoft's AI revenue may be bigger than reported. A new coding-focused model could accelerate uptake of tools like GitHub Copilot, which charges businesses per user per month. Good news for MSFT holders.

stories.title: All major AI models violate EU regulations — study
stories.why_it_matters: A new study has found that every major AI model currently on the market — including those from OpenAI, Google, Anthropic and others — is in breach of the EU's AI Act (Europe's new set of rules for how AI must behave safely and transparently). This is a significant finding: it means the world's biggest AI companies are all technically operating illegally in Europe right now. For investors in GOOGL and MSFT, this creates regulatory risk — potential fines or forced changes to how their AI products work in a market of 450 million people.

stories.title: OpenAI and Anthropic dominate AI revenue — and communicate very differently
stories.why_it_matters: A new market analysis shows OpenAI and Anthropic are pulling away from the pack in terms of actual AI revenue — not just hype. The report also highlights how the two companies take very different approaches to public communication: OpenAI is flashy and consumer-focused, Anthropic is quieter and enterprise-focused. For GOOGL holders, this is a reminder that Google's Gemini is competing in a market where the top two revenue spots are held by rivals.

sport.summary: State of Origin is the talk of the sporting nation after Game 1 delivered one of the most dramatic finishes in the series' history. NRL Round 13 kicks off tomorrow night. AFL has its own controversy brewing over a baffling no-goal call.

stories.title: 'Greatest escape' — NSW make history in stunning Origin send-off drama
stories.why_it_matters: Game 1 of the 2026 State of Origin series delivered one of the most extraordinary results the series has ever seen. NSW pulled off what's being called the 'greatest escape' in Origin history after a send-off dramatically changed the game. The Ponga send-off is at the centre of the controversy — a fiery post-match debate erupted, with a former Blue clashing with reporters and the NRL handing down its official verdict on the incident. The ref-Bunker exchange has been described as 'startling' and Queensland fans are furious about how it unfolded.

stories.title: NRL Round 13 team lists confirmed
stories.why_it_matters: All Round 13 team lists are now confirmed. The round kicks off tomorrow night (Friday 29 May) with Sharks vs Sea Eagles at 8pm. The Dolphins, Rabbitohs and Titans are all on the bye this week. Broncos host the Dragons on Sunday at Suncorp Stadium — the local game to watch for Gold Coast fans. Panthers take on the Warriors Sunday evening.

stories.title: AFL baffled by 'extraordinary error' as Hawks seek please explain over no-goal
stories.why_it_matters: Hawthorn are furious after what the AFL world is calling an 'extraordinary error' — a legitimate goal was ruled a no-goal in a recent match, potentially costing the Hawks crucial points. The club has formally requested a please explain from the AFL. The incident has left commentators and fans across the competition 'baffled', reigniting the ongoing debate about the reliability of the AFL's goal review technology and officiating standards.

stories.title: Origin fallout: biggest loser, unexpected winners and the real aftermath
stories.why_it_matters: CODE Sports has dug into the real fallout from Origin Game 1 beyond just the result. The send-off drama involving Ponga is identified as the pivotal moment, with analysis of who truly lost out (Queensland and their selection calls) and who emerged as surprise beneficiaries on the NSW side. The piece also looks at what the result means for the series and how both camps will approach Game 2.

watch_today.title: MSFT: Hold — AI tailwind is real
watch_today.detail: Microsoft jumped 3.3% last night and the fundamental story keeps getting stronger. New AI coding model at Build, analysts saying AI revenue is probably being underreported, and Azure cloud growth all point in the right direction. No reason to sell — but after a big single-night move, don't chase it either. Hold and let the story play out.

watch_today.title: CBA.AX: Hold — softer rates are a double-edged sword
watch_today.detail: CBA dropped 2% to $161.41 today. The RBA rate story is the driver — fewer rate hikes sounds good but can squeeze what banks earn on loans over time. CBA is still trading at a hefty premium to its actual value by most measures. No need to panic-sell today's dip, but equally no screaming reason to add more at this price.

watch_today.title: VGE.AX: Hold — emerging markets drag continues
watch_today.detail: Down 1.6% today to $91.50. Emerging markets are sensitive to global jitters and a stronger USD. No specific bad news — just broader pressure. If you're long-term on emerging markets, stay the course.

watch_today.title: EU AI regulations: watch the GOOGL and MSFT risk
watch_today.detail: A new study found every major AI model — including Google's Gemini and Microsoft's Copilot — is technically in breach of EU AI regulations. The EU has 450 million consumers and real teeth when it comes to fines (they've hit Google before for billions). This is a slow-burn risk worth keeping an eye on over coming months as enforcement ramps up.

watch_today.title: Gold surging — safe haven demand rising
watch_today.detail: Gold jumped over 2% last night to $4,537 USD/oz. When gold moves this sharply it usually signals that big investors are nervous about something — could be Middle East tensions, US debt concerns, or broader uncertainty. Not a direct portfolio move today but worth watching as a signal of where global risk appetite is heading.

watch_today.title: TTWO: Hold — GTA 6 narrative intact
watch_today.detail: Take-Two's CEO is talking confidently about GTA 6 not cannibalising GTA Online revenue, and says there's 'a lot of work to do' post-launch — hinting at years of DLC and monetisation ahead. The stock barely moved last night. The GTA 6 release is the big catalyst — sit tight.
